## Statement

With the notation of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]:

**(1) The dual action is an action by linear maps.** For all $w_1,w_2\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ one has $\mathrm{id}\cdot f=f$ and $w_1\cdot(w_2\cdot f)=(w_1w_2)\cdot f$, and for each $w$ the map $f\mapsto w\cdot f$ is linear.

**(2) The faces are nonempty.** Let $f_s\in V^*$ be the dual basis functionals of the basis $(e_s)$ of $V$, i.e. $f_s(e_t)=\delta_{st}$ ([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]). For $I\subseteq S$ the functional $f_I:=\sum_{s\notin I}f_s$ satisfies $f_I(e_s)=1$ for $s\notin I$ and $f_I(e_s)=0$ for $s\in I$; hence $f_I\in C_I$ and every face is nonempty. In particular $C^\circ\ni\sum_{s\in S}f_s$ is nonempty and $C_S=\{0\}$.

**(3) Rank two.** Let $s\ne t$ in $S$ and put $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$. Let $P^*:=\mathrm{Hom}(P,\mathbb R)$ be the algebraic dual space of the $2$-dimensional space $P$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), with the dual basis $f_s,f_t$ of the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ of $P$; functionals on $P$ are the restrictions of functionals on $V$. For $w\in W$ and $\varphi\in P^*$ define $(w\cdot\varphi)(v):=\varphi(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$ for $v\in P$; this is a left action of $W$ on the $2$-dimensional space $P^*$ by linear maps, the contragredient of the restriction of $\rho$ to $P$. Let $W_{s,t}:=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle\subseteq\mathrm{GL}(V)$. Writing $c:=c(s,t)$ (so $c=1$ for $m(s,t)=\infty$) and coordinates $(y_s,y_t)$ on $P^*$, so that $\varphi=y_sf_s+y_tf_t$ and $\varphi(e_s)=y_s$, $\varphi(e_t)=y_t$, the dual generators act by $$\rho(s)^*(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,\ 2cy_s+y_t),\qquad \rho(t)^*(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2cy_t,\ -y_t);$$ each is an involution fixing the line $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s)=0\}=\{y_s=0\}$ pointwise, respectively $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}=\{y_t=0\}$, and the functional $\delta(\varphi):=\varphi(e_s+e_t)$ is preserved by $W_{s,t}$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$. For $\beta\in P$ the rank-two root hyperplane is $H_\beta\cap P^*:=\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(\beta)=0\}$, and $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}\subset P$ is the rank-two root system.

(i) If $m:=m(s,t)<\infty$: $W_{s,t}$ is a dihedral group of order $2m$, and the $2m$ chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$), where $C_P:=\{f\in P^*:f(e_s)\ge0,\ f(e_t)\ge0\}$, are exactly the $2m$ closed sectors cut out in $P^*$ by the $m$ root hyperplanes $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}$. They have pairwise disjoint interiors, their union is all of $P^*$, $W_{s,t}$ acts simply transitively on them, and any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane, i.e. there is $\beta\in\Phi_P$ with the two interiors in opposite open half-planes of $H_\beta$.

(ii) If $m(s,t)=\infty$: the chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$) have pairwise disjoint interiors and their union is $\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(e_s+e_t)>0\}\cup\{0\}$, that is, the closed half-plane $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)\ge0\}$ with the nonzero points of its boundary line removed; any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, and the traces $H_\beta\cap\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)=1\}$ are exactly the integers in the coordinate $y_s$ on that affine line.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** a finite set $S$, a Coxeter matrix $m$, the space $V=\mathbb R^S$, the Coxeter form $B$, the reflections $r_a$, the presented group $W$, the canonical homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ with roots $\Phi$, and the dual action, chambers, faces and root hyperplanes on $V^*$ of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]; for distinct $s,t\in S$ the plane $P=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$ and the number $c=c(s,t)$.

[F1] $B(e_s,e_s)=1$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-c$ for all $s,t$; for $B(a,a)\ne0$ the map $r_a$ is a linear involution preserving $B$ with $r_a(a)=-a$ and $r_a$ the identity on $\ker B(-,a)$; for $a=e_s$ this gives $r_s(e_s)=-e_s$ and $r_s(e_t)=e_t+2ce_s$, and symmetrically $r_t(e_t)=-e_t$, $r_t(e_s)=e_s+2ce_t$; and for finite $m(s,t)$ the restriction $B|_P$ is positive definite ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]], [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]], clauses (2) and (3)(i)).

[F2] $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ is the unique homomorphism with $\rho(s)=r_s$ for $s\in S$, it satisfies $\rho(gh)=\rho(g)\rho(h)$ and $\rho(g^{-1})=\rho(g)^{-1}$, every $\rho(w)$ preserves $B$, and $\rho(wsw^{-1})=r_{\rho(w)e_s}$ for all $w\in W$, $s\in S$, so all reflections of $W$ act as the reflections in the roots $\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]], clauses (1), (2) and (4)).

[F3] The dual action is $(w\cdot f)(v)=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$; the closed chamber is $C=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)\ge0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$, its interior is $C^\circ=\{f:f(e_s)>0\text{ for all }s\}$, the face of type $I$ is $C_I=\{f:f(e_s)=0\text{ for }s\in I,\ f(e_s)>0\text{ for }s\notin I\}$, and $H_\alpha=\{f\in V^*:f(\alpha)=0\}$ for $\alpha\in\Phi$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]).

[F4] For a finite-dimensional space the dual space, the dual family of a basis and its basis property are as recorded in the algebraic-dual and dual-basis items; in particular $f_s(e_t)=\delta_{st}$ defines unique elements $f_s$ of the dual of $P$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]], [[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]).

[F5] $V=\mathbb R^S$ consists of the functions $S\to\mathbb R$ with pointwise operations, the functions $e_s$ form a basis of $V$, and $u=\sum_{s\in S}u(s)e_s$ for $u\in V$ ([[def-function-space]], [[def-linear-basis]]).

[F6] Trigonometric facts: the addition formulas; $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$; $\sin x=0$ if and only if $x\in\pi\mathbb Z$, and $\cos x=0$ if and only if $x=(k+\frac12)\pi$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$; $\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x$, $\cos\pi=-1$; $\cos 2x=\cos^2x-\sin^2x$ and $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$ follow from the addition formulas ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]).

[F7] $\pi>0$ and $\mathbb R$ is a totally ordered field, so $0<\pi/m\le\pi/2$ for $m\ge2$ and the order arithmetic below is the order of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]], [[thm-reals-ordered-field]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** first the action and face identities, then the explicit two-dimensional model, then the finite and infinite chamber computations.

1.1 The dual action is an action by linear maps. For $w\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ the formula $(w\cdot f)(v)=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$ defines an element of $V^*$ because a composite of linear maps is linear, and $f\mapsto w\cdot f$ is linear because evaluation at $v$ is linear in $f$. Moreover $\mathrm{id}\cdot f=f$, since $\rho(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, and $$w_1\cdot(w_2\cdot f)=f\circ\rho(w_2)^{-1}\circ\rho(w_1)^{-1}=f\circ\rho(w_1w_2)^{-1}=(w_1w_2)\cdot f,$$ using $\rho(w_1w_2)=\rho(w_1)\rho(w_2)$ and hence $\rho(w_1w_2)^{-1}=\rho(w_2)^{-1}\rho(w_1)^{-1}$. The same formula with $v$ restricted to $P$ defines a left action of $W$ on $P^*=\mathrm{Hom}(P,\mathbb R)$ by linear maps, the contragredient of $W\to\mathrm{GL}(P)$, $w\mapsto\rho(w)|_P$. [given, F2, F3, F4]

1.2 Generators on the dual plane. With $W$ acting on $P^*$ as in 1.1, the dual basis vectors satisfy $(s\cdot f_s)(e_s)=f_s(\rho(s)^{-1}e_s)=f_s(-e_s)=-1$ and $(s\cdot f_s)(e_t)=f_s(\rho(s)e_t)=f_s(e_t+2ce_s)=2c$, while $(s\cdot f_t)(e_s)=f_t(-e_s)=0$ and $(s\cdot f_t)(e_t)=f_t(e_t+2ce_s)=1$; hence in coordinates $s\cdot(y_sf_s+y_tf_t)=(-y_s)f_s+(2cy_s+y_t)f_t$, that is $$\rho(s)^*(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,\ 2cy_s+y_t).$$ The same computation with $s$ replaced by $t$ gives $\rho(t)^*(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2cy_t,\ -y_t)$. Both displayed maps are involutions: applying the first twice returns $(y_s,y_t)$, and applying the second twice returns $(y_s,y_t)$. The first fixes the line $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s)=0\}=\{y_s=0\}$ pointwise and the second fixes $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}=\{y_t=0\}$ pointwise, since these are exactly the vectors whose coordinate in question vanishes. For the functional $\delta(\varphi)=\varphi(e_s+e_t)=y_s+y_t$ one has $\delta(s\cdot\varphi)=(2c-1)y_s+y_t$ and $\delta(t\cdot\varphi)=y_s+(2c-1)y_t$, so each generator preserves $\delta$ exactly when $c=1$, i.e. when $m(s,t)=\infty$; in that case $W_{s,t}$ preserves $\delta$ because it is generated by $s$ and $t$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.3 Faces. Let $I\subseteq S$ and put $f_I:=\sum_{s\notin I}f_s\in V^*$. By the dual-basis property $f_I(e_s)=1$ for $s\notin I$ and $f_I(e_s)=0$ for $s\in I$; hence $f_I\in C_I$ and every face is nonempty. In particular $I=\varnothing$ gives $\sum_{s\in S}f_s\in C^\circ$, so the interior is nonempty, and $I=S$ gives $C_S=\{f:f(e_s)=0\text{ for all }s\in S\}=\{0\}$, since a functional vanishing on the basis $(e_s)$ of $V$ is zero. [given, F4, F5]

1.4 The finite rank-two model. Assume $m<\infty$ and put $\theta:=\pi/m$ and $c=\cos\theta$. Then $0<\theta\le\pi/2$, $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $1-c^2=\sin^2\theta$. On $P$ put $u:=e_s$ and $v:=(e_t+ce_s)/\sin\theta$. Then $B(u,u)=B(e_s,e_s)=1$, $B(u,v)=(B(e_s,e_t)+cB(e_s,e_s))/\sin\theta=(-c+c)/\sin\theta=0$ and $B(v,v)=(B(e_t,e_t)+2cB(e_s,e_t)+c^2B(e_s,e_s))/\sin^2\theta=(1-2c^2+c^2)/\sin^2\theta=(1-c^2)/\sin^2\theta=1$: thus $(u,v)$ is a $B|_P$-orthonormal basis of $P$ and $e_s=u$, $e_t=-cu+\sin\theta\,v$. Since $r_s$ fixes $\ker B(-,e_s)\cap P=\mathbb Rv$ pointwise and sends $u=e_s$ to $-u$, in the coordinates $(x_u,x_v)$ of the basis $(u,v)$ it is $r_s(x_u,x_v)=(-x_u,x_v)$; since $\ker B(-,e_t)\cap P$ is spanned by $(\sin\theta,c)$ and $r_t(e_t)=-e_t$, the map $r_t$ is the reflection in the line $\mathbb R(\sin\theta,c)$. Consequently the composite $A:=r_sr_t$ satisfies $A(u)=r_s(e_s+2ce_t)=r_s\bigl((1-2c^2)u+2c\sin\theta\,v\bigr)=(2c^2-1)u+2c\sin\theta\,v=(\cos2\theta)u+(\sin2\theta)v$ and $A(v)=-\sin2\theta\,u+\cos2\theta\,v$, so in the orthonormal coordinates $$A(x_u,x_v)=(x_u\cos2\theta-x_v\sin2\theta,\ x_u\sin2\theta+x_v\cos2\theta),$$ the rotation through $2\theta$, whose order is exactly $m$. [given, F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 The rank-two roots. Assume $m<\infty$ and keep the orthonormal coordinates $(u,v)$ of 1.4, in which $A$ is the rotation through $2\theta$; write a vector of $P$ as $\cos\varphi\,u+\sin\varphi\,v$ with $\varphi$ real. Then $A^k e_s=(\cos2k\theta)u+(\sin2k\theta)v$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, and $r_sA^ke_s=(-\cos2k\theta)u+(\sin2k\theta)v=(\cos(m-2k)\theta)u+(\sin(m-2k)\theta)v$ because $\pi=m\theta$ and $\cos(\pi-\alpha)=-\cos\alpha$, $\sin(\pi-\alpha)=\sin\alpha$. Moreover $e_t=-\cos\theta\,u+\sin\theta\,v=(\cos(m-1)\theta)u+(\sin(m-1)\theta)v$, and the same two formulas applied to $e_t$ give $A^ke_t$ and $r_sA^ke_t$ at angles $(m-1+2k)\theta$ and $(1-2k)\theta$. As $k$ varies over $\mathbb Z$ the angles $2k\theta$ are exactly the even multiples of $\theta$ and the angles $(1-2k)\theta$ are exactly the odd multiples, so every element of $S:=\{(\cos j\theta)u+(\sin j\theta)v:j=0,1,\dots,2m-1\}$ is one of the four displayed families and $S\subseteq\Phi_P$; conversely $S$ contains $e_s$ and $e_t$ and is stable under $A$ (which adds $2\theta$ to an angle) and under $r_s$ (which sends an angle $\varphi$ to $\pi-\varphi=(m\theta-\varphi)$), hence stable under $W_{s,t}=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle=\langle\rho(s),A\rangle$, so $\Phi_P\subseteq S$. Therefore $$\Phi_P=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}=\{(\cos j\theta)u+(\sin j\theta)v:\ j=0,1,\dots,2m-1\},$$ a set of exactly $2m$ unit vectors, and $\Phi_P$ is stable under $\beta\mapsto-\beta$. [given, F1, F2, F6, step 1.4]

2.2 The infinite case. Assume $m=\infty$, so $c=1$ and by 1.2 the generators act by $s\cdot(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,2y_s+y_t)$ and $t\cdot(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2y_t,-y_t)$ and preserve $\delta=y_s+y_t$. On the affine line $\{\delta=1\}$ parametrized by $\tau=y_s$ these maps read $\tau\mapsto-\tau$ and $\tau\mapsto2-\tau$, the two reflections of the line about $0$ and $1$. Hence the images of the interval $[0,1]$ under $W_{s,t}$ are exactly the unit intervals $[k,k+1]$, $k\in\mathbb Z$: the two given maps send $[0,1]$ to $[-1,0]$ and $[1,2]$, and conjugating by further elements and applying the same two maps produces exactly the remaining unit intervals, by induction on $|k|$. Since $C_P$ is the cone on $[0,1]$ in the half-plane $\{\delta\ge0\}$ and the action is linear, the chamber $wC_P$ is the cone on the interval corresponding to $w$; these cones have pairwise disjoint interiors and their union is $\{\varphi:\delta(\varphi)>0\}\cup\{0\}$, because every point with $\delta>0$ is a positive multiple of a unique point of $\{\delta=1\}$ lying in a unit interval, while every point of a cone on a unit interval has $\delta\ge0$ and only $0$ has $\delta=0$. The roots are $\beta=(a,b)$ with $a-b=\pm1$ (the orbits computed as in 2.1 with $A=I+N$), and a root hyperplane $H_\beta$ cuts the affine line $\{\delta=1\}$ at $y_s=b/(b-a)$, which equals $-b$ when $a-b=1$ and $b$ when $a-b=-1$, so the traces are exactly the integers; two distinct chambers, being cones on distinct unit intervals, are separated by the wall whose trace is the integer between those intervals. [given, F1, F2, F6, step 1.2]

3.1 The rank-two walls. Assume $m<\infty$. The map $\flat:P\to P^*$, $x\mapsto B(x,\cdot)$, is an isomorphism, because $B|_P$ is positive definite: if $B(x,\cdot)=0$ then $B(x,x)=0$ and $x=0$. For $\beta\in P$ one has $\flat(\beta^\perp)=H_\beta\cap P^*$, where $\beta^\perp=\{x\in P:B(x,\beta)=0\}$: indeed $\flat(x)(\beta)=B(x,\beta)$ vanishes exactly when $x\in\beta^\perp$. By 2.1 each $\beta\in\Phi_P$ is a unit vector at an angle $j\theta$, so $\beta^\perp$ is the line at angle $j\theta+\pi/2$, and the lines $H_\beta\cap P^*$ depend only on the pair $\{\beta,-\beta\}$: there are exactly $m$ of them, at angles $\pi/2+j\theta$, $j=0,\dots,m-1$, equally spaced by $\theta$. The chamber $C_P=\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(e_s)\ge0,\ \varphi(e_t)\ge0\}$ corresponds under $\flat$ to $\{x\in P:B(x,e_s)\ge0,\ B(x,e_t)\ge0\}$, whose boundary lines are $e_s^\perp$ (the line at angle $\pi/2$) and $e_t^\perp$ (the line at angle $(m-1)\theta+\pi/2$, i.e. $\pi/2-\theta$): so $C_P=\flat$ of the closed sector between these two consecutive walls, of angle $\theta$, and no root hyperplane line meets $C_P^\circ$ because the $m$ walls are equally spaced by $\theta$ and contain both boundary lines. [given, F1, F2, F3, F6, step 1.4, step 2.1]

4.1 The finite chamber tiling. Assume $m<\infty$. The group $W_{s,t}=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle$ generated by the two involutions $\rho(s),\rho(t)$ whose product $A$ has exact order $m$ is a quotient of the dihedral group of order $2m$, so $|W_{s,t}|\le2m$; on the other hand its action on $P^*$ contains the rotation $A$ of order $m$ and the reflection $\rho(s)$ in the wall $H_{e_s}\cap P^*$ by 1.4 and 3.1, and these generate a group of order exactly $2m$ acting on the $2m$ sectors of 3.1, so $|W_{s,t}|=2m$ and $W_{s,t}$ is dihedral of order $2m$. The action maps the set of $m$ walls to itself, because $\rho(w)(H_\beta\cap P^*)=H_{\rho(w)\beta}\cap P^*$ and $\Phi_P$ is $W_{s,t}$-stable, so it permutes the $2m$ closed sectors; it maps the sector $C_P$ to the sectors obtained by successive rotations through $2\theta$ and by the reflection $\rho(s)$, which realizes all $2m$ of them, so the orbit of $C_P$ is exactly the set of closed sectors cut out by the $m$ root hyperplanes. Since $|W_{s,t}|=2m$ equals the number of sectors, the action on the orbit is simply transitive, and the sectors have pairwise disjoint interiors and union $P^*$ as the $2m$ sectors of $m$ distinct lines through the origin. Finally, any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane: choosing points $p,q$ in their interiors, the segment from $p$ to $q$ crosses some wall line $H_\beta\cap P^*$ (the interiors are different connected components of the complement of the union of the walls), and the two open half-planes of that line are convex and disjoint, so $p$ and $q$ lie in opposite open half-planes. [given, F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

items.title: The real Coxeter form, its radical, reflections, and form-preserving maps
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set and let $m$ be a Coxeter matrix on $S$, so that $m(s,s)=1$ and $m(s,t)=m(t,s)\in\{2,3,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ for $s\ne t$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]).

**(1) The space and its distinguished functions.** Let $V:=\mathbb R^S$ be the real vector space of all functions $S\to\mathbb R$, with pointwise operations ([[def-function-space]]); it is a vector space over the ordered field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]). Write $u(s)$ for the value of $u$ at $s$ and put $e_s(s):=1$, $e_s(t):=0$ for $t\ne s$.

**(2) The Coxeter form.** For finite $m(s,t)$ put $c(s,t):=\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ ([[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]]) and for $m(s,t)=\infty$ put $c(s,t):=1$; then $c(s,t)=c(t,s)$ and $c(s,s)=\cos\pi=-1$. The **Coxeter form** $B$ is the unique symmetric bilinear form on $V$ with $B(e_s,e_t)=-c(s,t)$ for all $s,t\in S$; in particular $B(e_s,e_s)=1$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ for finite $m(s,t)$, while $B(e_s,e_t)=-1$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]], [[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]]). **No positive definiteness, definiteness or nondegeneracy of $B$ is presumed**: $\operatorname{rad}(B):=\{u:B(u,v)=0\text{ for all }v\in V\}$ may be nonzero ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and the form may be indefinite ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]). A linear map $g:V\to V$ is **$B$-preserving** when $B(gu,gw)=B(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$.

**(3) Reflections.** For $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$ define the **reflection with normal $a$** by $$r_a(v):=v-\frac{2B(v,a)}{B(a,a)}a .$$ The definition asserts neither that $r_a$ is linear or an involution nor that $\ker B(-,a)=\{v:B(v,a)=0\}$ is a hyperplane; these are proved in [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]. When $B(a,a)=0$ the symbol $r_a$ is not defined.
items.strategy: A definition item; the only substantive assertions are the bilinearity and uniqueness of $B$ and the elementary basis property of the $e_s$. Since $S$ is finite, $\sum_s\lambda_se_s=0$ evaluated at $s$ gives $\lambda_s=0$, so the $e_s$ are independent, and $u=\sum_su(s)e_s$ is a finite sum, so they span; hence a bilinear form is determined by its values on pairs of basis vectors, and the correspondence between bilinear forms and linear maps $V\to V^*$ ([[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]]) together with the basis property supplies existence and uniqueness of $B$; both facts are restated as the opening clause of [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]], which is this definition's recorded justifier. Symmetry of $B$ follows from $m(s,t)=m(t,s)$ and from $c(s,t)=c(t,s)$; the diagonal value is $B(e_s,e_s)=-\cos(\pi/1)=-\cos\pi=1$ ([[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] is the companion record of $\cos\pi=-1$; the sine/cosine definition items fix the functions). The reflection formula is a definition of a vector $r_a(v)\in V$ for each pair $(v,a)$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$; linearity and the reflection identities are deliberately not asserted here and are established by the justifier. The page's central warning is preserved: no Euclidean structure, positive definiteness or invertibility of the Gram matrix is presumed. No Choice is used: $S$ is finite and all selections are finite.

items.title: Reflections: involutivity, form invariance, fixed hyperplane, and exact rank-two order
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V=\mathbb R^S$, $B$ and $r_a$ be as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]].

**(1) Well-definedness of $B$.** The functions $e_s$ ($s\in S$) form a basis of $V$, and there is exactly one symmetric bilinear form $B$ on $V$ with $B(e_s,e_t)=-\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ for finite $m(s,t)$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-1$ for $m(s,t)=\infty$; it satisfies $B(u,w)=\sum_{s,t\in S}u(s)w(t)B(e_s,e_t)$ for all $u,w\in V$.

**(2) Reflection identities.** Let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$. Then $r_a$ is linear, $r_a^2=\mathrm{id}_V$, $r_a(a)=-a$, $r_a(v)=v$ for every $v$ with $B(v,a)=0$, and $B(r_au,r_aw)=B(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$. Moreover $\ker B(-,a)$ is a linear subspace of dimension $\dim V-1$ (a hyperplane of $V$, in the codimension-one sense) and is fixed pointwise by $r_a$.

**(3) The rank-two plane.** Let $s\ne t$ in $S$, put $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$ and $c:=c(s,t)$ as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (so $c=1$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$). Then:

(i) $B|_P$ has Gram matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&-c\\-c&1\end{pmatrix}$; for finite $m$ it is positive definite, with $B(x_se_s+x_te_t,\,x_se_s+x_te_t)=(x_s-cx_t)^2+\sin^2(\pi/m)\,x_t^2$; for $m=\infty$ it is positive semidefinite, i.e. $B(x,x)\ge0$ for all $x\in P$, with radical $\mathbb R(e_s+e_t)$.

(ii) $r_s$ and $r_t$ fix every element of $P^\perp=\{v\in V:B(v,e_s)=B(v,e_t)=0\}$ pointwise; and if $m<\infty$ then $V=P\oplus P^\perp$.

(iii) The product $A:=r_sr_t$ has, in the ordered basis $(e_s,e_t)$ of $P$, the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}4c^2-1&-2c\\2c&-1\end{pmatrix}$, of determinant $1$.

(iv) If $m<\infty$ then $\operatorname{tr}A=2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $A^m=\mathrm{id}_V$, and $A^k\ne\mathrm{id}_V$ for $0<k<m$. If $m=\infty$ then $A=\mathrm{id}_P+N$ on $P$ for some $N$ with $N\ne0$ and $N^2=0$; hence $(r_sr_t)^k|_P=\mathrm{id}_P+kN$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, so $r_sr_t$ has infinite order on $V$.

items.title: The canonical reflection homomorphism, roots, reflections, and the positive cone
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$ be as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]], let $W$ be the presented Coxeter group of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]] with its universal property, and put $r_s:=r_{e_s}$ for $s\in S$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]).

**(1)** Write $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ for the group of invertible linear maps $V\to V$, the unit group of the monoid of linear endomorphisms under composition ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]], [[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]], [[lem-monoid-units-form-a-group]]). The **canonical reflection homomorphism** is the group homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ ([[def-group-homomorphism]]) that satisfies $\rho(s)=r_s$ for every $s\in S$; its existence and uniqueness are established by [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]], which is this definition's recorded justifier. For $w\in W$ and $v\in V$ write $\rho(w)v$ for the image.

**(2)** The **root system** of the pair is $\Phi:=\{\rho(w)e_s:w\in W,\ s\in S\}\subset V$; its elements are the **roots**. The set of **reflections** of $W$ is $T:=\{wsw^{-1}:w\in W,\ s\in S\}\subset W$; that $\rho(wsw^{-1})$ is the reflection $r_{\rho(w)e_s}$ and that every root is $B$-non-isotropic are proved in [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]].

**(3)** The **positive cone** is $V_+:=\{\sum_{s\in S}\lambda_se_s:\lambda_s\in\mathbb R,\ \lambda_s\ge0\}$ and the **negative cone** is $-V_+$ ([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]).

No positivity of $\rho(w)e_s$ for fixed $w$, no faithfulness or injectivity of $\rho$, no discreteness and no nondegeneracy of $B$ is asserted by this definition.
items.strategy: A definition item. Every symbol names an object already constructed: $V$, $B$, the $e_s$ and $r_s$ come from the previous items of this page, and $W$ with its presentation and universal property comes from [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]; $\rho$ is defined by its values on the generating set $S$, and the well-definedness obligation (that the generator assignment satisfies the presentation's relators, so that the universal property yields a unique homomorphism) is exactly what the recorded justifier [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] proves. $\Phi$, $T$, $V_+$ and $-V_+$ are set definitions, and the membership of roots in the non-isotropic locus, and the identification $\rho(wsw^{-1})=r_{\rho(w)e_s}$, are attributed to the justifier rather than asserted here. The stated abstentions (no positivity, faithfulness, discreteness or nondegeneracy) preserve the design's warning that these are conclusions of later pages, not part of this definition. No Choice is used.

items.title: Descent of the reflection representation, unit root norms, and conjugation of reflections
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$, $W$, $r_s$, $\rho$, $\Phi$, $T$ be as in [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]].

**(1) Relators and descent.** For every $s\in S$ one has $r_s^2=\mathrm{id}_V$, and for all $s\ne t$ with $m(s,t)<\infty$ one has $(r_sr_t)^{m(s,t)}=\mathrm{id}_V$. Consequently the assignment $s\mapsto r_s$ sends every relator of the presentation to the identity, and by the universal property of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]] there is a **unique** group homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ with $\rho(s)=r_s$ for all $s\in S$.

**(2) $\rho$ preserves the form.** For every $w\in W$ and all $u,w'\in V$, $B(\rho(w)u,\rho(w)w')=B(u,w')$.

**(3) Roots have unit norm.** For every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$, $B(\rho(w)e_s,\rho(w)e_s)=1$; hence every root $\alpha\in\Phi$ satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=1\ne0$ and $r_\alpha$ is defined.

**(4) Conjugation of reflections.** Let $g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$ be $B$-preserving and let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$. Then $gr_ag^{-1}=r_{ga}$. In particular, for every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$, $$\rho(wsw^{-1})=\rho(w)r_s\rho(w)^{-1}=r_{\rho(w)e_s},$$ so every $t=wsw^{-1}\in T$ acts on $V$ as the reflection in the root $\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi$.
items.strategy: (1) $r_s^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $B$-invariance of each $r_s$ are [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (2); the exact rank-two orders give $(r_sr_t)^{m(s,t)}=\mathrm{id}$. These are precisely the relators of the presented group, so the map $S\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $s\mapsto r_s$ satisfies the hypotheses of the universal property ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), which yields a homomorphism $\rho$; uniqueness holds because $S$ generates $W$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]). (2) Each generator preserves $B$, and a composite of $B$-preserving maps preserves $B$. (3) $B(\rho(w)e_s,\rho(w)e_s)=B(e_s,e_s)=1$ by (2) and $B(e_s,e_s)=1$. (4) Let $g$ preserve $B$. Then $B(ga,ga)=B(a,a)$ and $B(g^{-1}v,a)=B(v,ga)$, so $r_{ga}(v)=v-\frac{2B(g^{-1}v,a)}{B(a,a)}ga=g\bigl(g^{-1}v-\frac{2B(g^{-1}v,a)}{B(a,a)}a\bigr)=gr_ag^{-1}(v)$ for all $v$; substituting $g=\rho(w)$, $a=e_s$ and using $\rho(s)=r_s$ gives the displayed conjugation identity. No Choice is used.

items.title: The dual action, chambers, faces, and root hyperplanes
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$, $W$, $\rho$, $\Phi$ be as in [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], and let $V^*$ be the algebraic dual of $V$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**(1) The dual action.** For $w\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ define $w\cdot f\in V^*$ by $$(w\cdot f)(v):=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v).$$ This is the dual (contragredient) action of $\rho$; that it really is a left action by linear maps is proved in [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]]. **The dual action is used even when $B$ is degenerate**: no identification of $V$ with $V^*$ through $B$ is made or assumed.

**(2) Chambers, faces, root hyperplanes.** The **closed chamber** is $C:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)\ge0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$, its **interior** is $C^\circ:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$, and for $I\subseteq S$ the **face** $C_I$ is $$C_I:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)=0\text{ for }s\in I\text{ and }f(e_s)>0\text{ for }s\notin I\},$$ the set of functionals of $C$ vanishing exactly on $I$. For a root $\alpha\in\Phi$ the **root hyperplane** is $H_\alpha:=\{f\in V^*:f(\alpha)=0\}=\ker(\mathrm{ev}_\alpha)$, the kernel of the evaluation functional $f\mapsto f(\alpha)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]).

Neither the nonemptiness of the $C_I$ nor any orbit or tiling property is asserted here; existence of the faces and the exact rank-two chamber structure are proved in [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]].
items.strategy: A definition item. $V^*$ is the published algebraic dual ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]); since $\rho(w)$ is invertible ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]]), the formula $(w\cdot f)(v)=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$ defines an element of $V^*$ for each $w,f$, and the action axioms are not asserted but delegated to the recorded justifier [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]]. The closed chamber $C$ and its faces are the standard Tits-cone chamber of the dual (geometric) representation (Davis Appendix D.1); the root hyperplanes are the kernels of the evaluation functionals at roots (a hyperplane is the kernel of a nonzero functional, [[def-linear-subspace]], [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). The design's explicit warning is kept: the dual action is required even when $B$ is degenerate, so no isomorphism $V\cong V^*$ induced by $B$ is used. No Choice is used.

items.title: The dual action, the faces, and the rank-two chamber tiling
items.statement:
With the notation of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]:

**(1) The dual action is an action by linear maps.** For all $w_1,w_2\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ one has $\mathrm{id}\cdot f=f$ and $w_1\cdot(w_2\cdot f)=(w_1w_2)\cdot f$, and for each $w$ the map $f\mapsto w\cdot f$ is linear.

**(2) The faces are nonempty.** Let $f_s\in V^*$ be the dual basis functionals of the basis $(e_s)$ of $V$, i.e. $f_s(e_t)=\delta_{st}$ ([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]). For $I\subseteq S$ the functional $f_I:=\sum_{s\notin I}f_s$ satisfies $f_I(e_s)=1$ for $s\notin I$ and $f_I(e_s)=0$ for $s\in I$; hence $f_I\in C_I$ and every face is nonempty. In particular $C^\circ\ni\sum_{s\in S}f_s$ is nonempty and $C_S=\{0\}$.

**(3) Rank two.** Let $s\ne t$ in $S$ and put $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$. Let $P^*:=\mathrm{Hom}(P,\mathbb R)$ be the algebraic dual space of the $2$-dimensional space $P$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), with the dual basis $f_s,f_t$ of the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ of $P$; functionals on $P$ are the restrictions of functionals on $V$. For $w\in W$ and $\varphi\in P^*$ define $(w\cdot\varphi)(v):=\varphi(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$ for $v\in P$; this is a left action of $W$ on the $2$-dimensional space $P^*$ by linear maps, the contragredient of the restriction of $\rho$ to $P$. Let $W_{s,t}:=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle\subseteq\mathrm{GL}(V)$. Writing $c:=c(s,t)$ (so $c=1$ for $m(s,t)=\infty$) and coordinates $(y_s,y_t)$ on $P^*$, so that $\varphi=y_sf_s+y_tf_t$ and $\varphi(e_s)=y_s$, $\varphi(e_t)=y_t$, the dual generators act by $$\rho(s)^*(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,\ 2cy_s+y_t),\qquad \rho(t)^*(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2cy_t,\ -y_t);$$ each is an involution fixing the line $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s)=0\}=\{y_s=0\}$ pointwise, respectively $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}=\{y_t=0\}$, and the functional $\delta(\varphi):=\varphi(e_s+e_t)$ is preserved by $W_{s,t}$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$. For $\beta\in P$ the rank-two root hyperplane is $H_\beta\cap P^*:=\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(\beta)=0\}$, and $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}\subset P$ is the rank-two root system.

(i) If $m:=m(s,t)<\infty$: $W_{s,t}$ is a dihedral group of order $2m$, and the $2m$ chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$), where $C_P:=\{f\in P^*:f(e_s)\ge0,\ f(e_t)\ge0\}$, are exactly the $2m$ closed sectors cut out in $P^*$ by the $m$ root hyperplanes $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}$. They have pairwise disjoint interiors, their union is all of $P^*$, $W_{s,t}$ acts simply transitively on them, and any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane, i.e. there is $\beta\in\Phi_P$ with the two interiors in opposite open half-planes of $H_\beta$.

(ii) If $m(s,t)=\infty$: the chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$) have pairwise disjoint interiors and their union is $\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(e_s+e_t)>0\}\cup\{0\}$, that is, the closed half-plane $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)\ge0\}$ with the nonzero points of its boundary line removed; any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, and the traces $H_\beta\cap\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)=1\}$ are exactly the integers in the coordinate $y_s$ on that affine line.
items.strategy: (1) The formula is precomposition with $\rho(w)^{-1}$, hence linear in $f$; associativity is $w_1\cdot(w_2\cdot f)=f\circ\rho(w_2)^{-1}\circ\rho(w_1)^{-1}=f\circ\rho((w_1w_2)^{-1})=(w_1w_2)\cdot f$, using that $\rho$ is a homomorphism ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]]). (2) Evaluate the proposed functional $f_I$ on $e_s$; the dual basis exists in finite dimension ([[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]). (3) The displayed formulas are the transposed inverses of the matrices of $\rho(s),\rho(t)$ in the basis $(e_s,e_t)$: $\rho(s)$ fixes $e_s$ up to sign and sends $e_t\mapsto e_t+2ce_s$, $\rho(t)$ acts symmetrically, and a dual matrix is the inverse transpose ([[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]], [[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). The finite case: $W_{s,t}$ is dihedral of order $2m$ because its two generators are involutions with product $\rho(s)\rho(t)$ of exact order $m$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]); on $P^*$ we use the positive definite form transported from $B|_P$ by the identification $e_s\mapsto f_s$ (equivalently $B^*$ with $B^*(f_s,f_t)=-c$, $B^*(f_s,f_s)=B^*(f_t,f_t)=1$), for which the two generators are orthogonal reflections in the lines $\{y_s=0\}$, $\{y_t=0\}$ whose angle is $\pi/m$: indeed the unit normals $\varphi_s=(1,-c)$, $\varphi_t=(-c,1)$ have $B^*(\varphi_s,\varphi_t)=-c=\cos(\pi-\pi/m)$ and cosine is strictly decreasing on $[0,\pi]$ ([[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]), while the sector angle identity for two half-planes with unit normals at angle $\psi$ is $\pi-\psi$. The product $\rho(s)\rho(t)$ is then a rotation of exact order $m$, the $m$ reflections of the dihedral group are exactly the $\rho$-images of the elements of $T\cap W_{s,t}$, and their $m$ fixed lines are the root hyperplanes $H_\beta\cap P^*$; the roots $\beta\in\Phi_P$ are the $2m$ vectors of the dihedral root system, whose directions are equally spaced by $\pi/m$ in the $B^*$ metric, and every root has $\beta_s\beta_t\ge0$ in the coordinates $(e_s,e_t)$: this is what makes $C_P^\circ$ disjoint from every root hyperplane. Hence $C_P^\circ$ is a connected component of the complement of the $m$ root lines and $C_P$ is one of the $2m$ closed sectors. The orbit map $w\mapsto wC_P$ is injective: an element preserving $C_P$ permutes its two extreme rays, a rotation doing so is the identity (a determinant-one orthogonal map of the plane fixing a nonzero vector), and the swap is the orthogonal reflection in the bisector line $B^*(\varphi_s+\varphi_t,\cdot)=0$, whose direction is not a root direction because the root directions are the $2m$ multiples of $\pi/m$ while the bisector direction is $(2m-1)\pi/(2m)$, not a multiple of $\pi/m$; the swap is therefore none of the $m$ reflections of $W_{s,t}$ (whose fixed lines are root hyperplanes). Since $|W_{s,t}|=2m$ equals the number of sectors, the orbit is the full set of $2m$ sectors and the tiling, simple transitivity and separation statements follow. The infinite case: with $c=1$, $\rho(s)$ and $\rho(t)$ preserve the functional $\delta:f\mapsto f(e_s+e_t)$, and on the affine line $\{f:\delta(f)=1\}$, parametrized by $y_s$, they act by $y_s\mapsto-y_s$ and $y_s\mapsto2-y_s$. Induction on the integer part gives that the images of the interval $[0,1]$ under this group are exactly the unit intervals $[j,j+1]$, $j\in\mathbb Z$, which cover $\mathbb R$ with pairwise disjoint interiors; the images of $H_{e_s}$ and $H_{e_t}$ are the integers. Taking cones over these intervals inside $\{\delta\ge0\}$ gives the stated tiling of the half-plane and the separation by root hyperplanes. This is the rank-two input used by the higher-rank chamber theory; the general Tits-cone theorems are not proved here. All arguments are finite-dimensional or explicit real computations; no Choice is used.

items.title: Reflection matrices in a positive plane, a Lorentzian plane, and a plane with radical
items.statement:
Let $B$ be a symmetric bilinear form on a real vector space $V$ and let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$; the formula $r_a(v)=v-\frac{2B(v,a)}{B(a,a)}a$ of [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] defines an involution preserving $B$, fixing $\ker B(-,a)$ pointwise ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]). In $V=\mathbb R^2$ with standard basis $e_1,e_2$ ([[def-function-space]], [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]) the following three cases are computed, each matrix being taken in the basis $(e_1,e_2)$ (inertia as in [[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]).

**(i) Positive plane.** $B$ the dot product, $a=\frac35e_1+\frac45e_2$, so $B(a,a)=1$. Then $r_a(e_1)=\frac7{25}e_1-\frac{24}{25}e_2$, $r_a(e_2)=-\frac{24}{25}e_1-\frac7{25}e_2$, i.e. $$[r_a]=\frac1{25}\begin{pmatrix}7&-24\\-24&-7\end{pmatrix},\qquad [r_a]^2=I_2,\qquad \det[r_a]=-1,$$ and $B$ has inertia $(2,0,0)$: a Euclidean reflection across the line $\mathbb R(-4e_1+3e_2)$.

**(ii) Lorentzian plane.** $B(x,y)=x_1y_1-x_2y_2$, of inertia $(1,1,0)$, and $a=2e_1+e_2$, so $B(a,a)=3$. Then $r_a(e_1)=-\frac53e_1-\frac43e_2$, $r_a(e_2)=\frac43e_1+\frac53e_2$, i.e. $$[r_a]=\frac13\begin{pmatrix}-5&4\\-4&5\end{pmatrix},\qquad [r_a]^2=I_2,\qquad \det[r_a]=-1,$$ and $[r_a]$ preserves $B$: $B(r_ae_1,r_ae_1)=1$, $B(r_ae_2,r_ae_2)=-1$, $B(r_ae_1,r_ae_2)=0$.

**(iii) Plane with radical.** $B(x,y)=x_1y_1$, of inertia $(1,0,1)$ and radical $\operatorname{rad}(B)=\mathbb Re_2$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and $a=e_1$: then $r_a=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, i.e. $r_a(e_1)=-e_1$ and $r_a(e_2)=e_2$, with fixed hyperplane $\ker B(-,e_1)=\mathbb Re_2=\operatorname{rad}(B)$. The vector $e_2$ is $B$-null, so the displayed formula does not define a reflection with normal $e_2$.

(i) $r_a(e_1)=e_1-2B(e_1,a)a=e_1-\frac65a=\frac7{25}e_1-\frac{24}{25}e_2$ and $r_a(e_2)=e_2-\frac85a=-\frac{24}{25}e_1-\frac7{25}e_2$; squaring the matrix gives $I_2$ and its determinant is $\frac{-49+576}{625}=-1$. (ii) $B(e_1,a)=2$ and $B(e_2,a)=-1$, so $r_a(e_1)=e_1-\frac43a$ and $r_a(e_2)=e_2+\frac23a$; the displayed entries follow and the invariance identities are the explicit evaluations of $x_1y_1-x_2y_2$. (iii) $B(-,e_1)=x_1$ is evaluation of the first coordinate, so $r_{e_1}(v)=v-2v_1e_1$; its kernel is the $e_2$-axis, which is also the radical because $B(e_2,\cdot)=0$. Each case verifies the general identities of [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] on explicit numbers, and the last sentence records the exact hypothesis $B(a,a)\ne0$ of the definition.

items.title: The finite dihedral rotation and the infinite unipotent rank-two product
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s,t\}$, $m=m(s,t)$, $V=\mathbb R^S$, $B$ the Coxeter form, $P=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$ and $c$ as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] ($c=1$ for $m=\infty$). By [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] the product $A:=r_sr_t$ acts on $P$ with matrix $$A=\begin{pmatrix}4c^2-1&-2c\\2c&-1\end{pmatrix}$$ in the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ ([[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]).

**(i) Finite dihedral rotation.** For $m=3$ one has $c=\cos(\pi/3)=\frac12$ and $$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^2=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^3=I_2,$$ so $A$ has order $3=m$; its trace is $-1=2\cos(2\pi/3)$, consistent with a rotation through $2\pi/3$ of the positive definite plane $(P,B|_P)$, and $A\ne I_2\ne A^2$. For $m=2$ the same formula gives $c=0$ and $A=-I_2$, of order $2=m$.

**(ii) Infinite unipotent product.** For $m=\infty$ one has $c=1$ and $$A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-2\\2&-1\end{pmatrix}=I_2+N,\qquad N=\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\2&-2\end{pmatrix}\ne0,\qquad N^2=0 .$$ Hence $A^k=I_2+kN$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, so $A^k(e_s)=e_s+2k(e_s+e_t)$ and no nonzero power of $A$ is the identity: the pair $(r_s,r_t)$ has infinite order, in contrast to the finite cases where $A$ has order $m$. In the abstract group $W$ of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], the element $st$ likewise has infinite order when $m=\infty$, and has order $m$ in the displayed finite cases $m=2,3$.

With $W$ acting on $P^*$ as in 1.1, the dual basis vectors satisfy $(s\cdot f_s)(e_s)=f_s(\rho(s)^{-1}e_s)=f_s(-e_s)=-1$ and $(s\cdot f_s)(e_t)=f_s(\rho(s)e_t)=f_s(e_t+2ce_s)=2c$, while $(s\cdot f_t)(e_s)=f_t(-e_s)=0$ and $(s\cdot f_t)(e_t)=f_t(e_t+2ce_s)=1$; hence in coordinates $s\cdot(y_sf_s+y_tf_t)=(-y_s)f_s+(2cy_s+y_t)f_t$, that is $$\rho(s)^*(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,\ 2cy_s+y_t).$$ The same computation with $s$ replaced by $t$ gives $\rho(t)^*(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2cy_t,\ -y_t)$. Both displayed maps are involutions: applying the first twice returns $(y_s,y_t)$, and applying the second twice returns $(y_s,y_t)$. The first fixes the line $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s)=0\}=\{y_s=0\}$ pointwise and the second fixes $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}=\{y_t=0\}$ pointwise, since these are exactly the vectors whose coordinate in question vanishes. For the functional $\delta(\varphi)=\varphi(e_s+e_t)=y_s+y_t$ one has $\delta(s\cdot\varphi)=(2c-1)y_s+y_t$ and $\delta(t\cdot\varphi)=y_s+(2c-1)y_t$, so each generator preserves $\delta$ exactly when $c=1$, i.e. when $m(s,t)=\infty$; in that case $W_{s,t}$ preserves $\delta$ because it is generated by $s$ and $t$.

The finite rank-two model. Assume $m<\infty$ and put $\theta:=\pi/m$ and $c=\cos\theta$. Then $0<\theta\le\pi/2$, $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $1-c^2=\sin^2\theta$. On $P$ put $u:=e_s$ and $v:=(e_t+ce_s)/\sin\theta$. Then $B(u,u)=B(e_s,e_s)=1$, $B(u,v)=(B(e_s,e_t)+cB(e_s,e_s))/\sin\theta=(-c+c)/\sin\theta=0$ and $B(v,v)=(B(e_t,e_t)+2cB(e_s,e_t)+c^2B(e_s,e_s))/\sin^2\theta=(1-2c^2+c^2)/\sin^2\theta=(1-c^2)/\sin^2\theta=1$: thus $(u,v)$ is a $B|_P$-orthonormal basis of $P$ and $e_s=u$, $e_t=-cu+\sin\theta\,v$. Since $r_s$ fixes $\ker B(-,e_s)\cap P=\mathbb Rv$ pointwise and sends $u=e_s$ to $-u$, in the coordinates $(x_u,x_v)$ of the basis $(u,v)$ it is $r_s(x_u,x_v)=(-x_u,x_v)$; since $\ker B(-,e_t)\cap P$ is spanned by $(\sin\theta,c)$ and $r_t(e_t)=-e_t$, the map $r_t$ is the reflection in the line $\mathbb R(\sin\theta,c)$. Consequently the composite $A:=r_sr_t$ satisfies $A(u)=r_s(e_s+2ce_t)=r_s\bigl((1-2c^2)u+2c\sin\theta\,v\bigr)=(2c^2-1)u+2c\sin\theta\,v=(\cos2\theta)u+(\sin2\theta)v$ and $A(v)=-\sin2\theta\,u+\cos2\theta\,v$, so in the orthonormal coordinates $$A(x_u,x_v)=(x_u\cos2\theta-x_v\sin2\theta,\ x_u\sin2\theta+x_v\cos2\theta),$$ the rotation through $2\theta$, whose order is exactly $m$.

The rank-two roots. Assume $m<\infty$ and keep the orthonormal coordinates $(u,v)$ of 1.4, in which $A$ is the rotation through $2\theta$; write a vector of $P$ as $\cos\varphi\,u+\sin\varphi\,v$ with $\varphi$ real. Then $A^k e_s=(\cos2k\theta)u+(\sin2k\theta)v$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, and $r_sA^ke_s=(-\cos2k\theta)u+(\sin2k\theta)v=(\cos(m-2k)\theta)u+(\sin(m-2k)\theta)v$ because $\pi=m\theta$ and $\cos(\pi-\alpha)=-\cos\alpha$, $\sin(\pi-\alpha)=\sin\alpha$. Moreover $e_t=-\cos\theta\,u+\sin\theta\,v=(\cos(m-1)\theta)u+(\sin(m-1)\theta)v$, and the same two formulas applied to $e_t$ give $A^ke_t$ and $r_sA^ke_t$ at angles $(m-1+2k)\theta$ and $(1-2k)\theta$. As $k$ varies, the angles $2k\theta$ and $(m-2k)\theta$ realize every even multiple of $\theta$ (for $m$ even both families are the even multiples), and the angles $(m-1+2k)\theta$ and $(1-2k)\theta$ realize every odd multiple of $\theta$ precisely when $m$ is even; when $m$ is odd the family $(m-2k)\theta$ already realizes every odd multiple. Hence $$\Phi_P=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}=\{(\cos j\theta)u+(\sin j\theta)v:\ j=0,1,\dots,2m-1\},$$ a set of exactly $2m$ unit vectors, and $\Phi_P$ is stable under $\beta\mapsto-\beta$.

The infinite case. Assume $m=\infty$, so $c=1$ and by 1.2 the generators act by $s\cdot(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,2y_s+y_t)$ and $t\cdot(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2y_t,-y_t)$ and preserve $\delta=y_s+y_t$. On the affine line $\{\delta=1\}$ parametrized by $\tau=y_s$ these maps read $\tau\mapsto-\tau$ and $\tau\mapsto2-\tau$, the two reflections of the line about $0$ and $1$. Hence the images of the interval $[0,1]$ under $W_{s,t}$ are exactly the unit intervals $[k,k+1]$, $k\in\mathbb Z$: the two given maps send $[0,1]$ to $[-1,0]$ and $[1,2]$, and conjugating by further elements and applying the same two maps produces exactly the remaining unit intervals, by induction on $|k|$. Since $C_P$ is the cone on $[0,1]$ in the half-plane $\{\delta\ge0\}$ and the action is linear, the chamber $wC_P$ is the cone on the interval corresponding to $w$; these cones have pairwise disjoint interiors and their union is $\{\varphi:\delta(\varphi)>0\}\cup\{0\}$, because every point with $\delta>0$ is a positive multiple of a unique point of $\{\delta=1\}$ lying in a unique unit interval, while every point of a cone on a unit interval has $\delta\ge0$ and only $0$ has $\delta=0$. The roots are $\beta=(a,b)$ with $a-b=\pm1$ (the orbits computed as in 2.1 with $A=I+N$), and a root hyperplane $H_\beta$ cuts the affine line $\{\delta=1\}$ at $y_s=b/(b-a)$, which for $a-b=1$ equals $-b$ and for $a-b=-1$ equals $a$, so the traces are exactly the integers; two distinct chambers, being cones on distinct unit intervals, are separated by the wall whose trace is the integer between those intervals.

The rank-two walls. Assume $m<\infty$. The map $\flat:P\to P^*$, $x\mapsto B(x,\cdot)$, is an isomorphism, because $B|_P$ is positive definite: if $B(x,\cdot)=0$ then $B(x,x)=0$ and $x=0$. For $\beta\in P$ one has $\flat(\beta^\perp)=H_\beta\cap P^*$, where $\beta^\perp=\{x\in P:B(x,\beta)=0\}$: indeed $\flat(x)(\beta)=B(x,\beta)$ vanishes exactly when $x\in\beta^\perp$. By 2.1 each $\beta\in\Phi_P$ is a unit vector at an angle $j\theta$, so $\beta^\perp$ is the line at angle $j\theta+\pi/2$, and the lines $H_\beta\cap P^*$ depend only on the pair $\{\beta,-\beta\}$: there are exactly $m$ of them, at angles $\pi/2+j\theta$, $j=0,\dots,m-1$, equally spaced by $\theta$. The chamber $C_P=\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(e_s)\ge0,\ \varphi(e_t)\ge0\}$ corresponds under $\flat$ to $\{x\in P:B(x,e_s)\ge0,\ B(x,e_t)\ge0\}$, whose boundary lines are $e_s^\perp$ (the line at angle $\pi/2$) and $e_t^\perp$ (the line at angle $(m-1)\theta+\pi/2$, i.e. $\pi/2-\theta$): so $C_P=\flat$ of the closed sector between these two consecutive walls, of angle $\theta$, and no root hyperplane line meets $C_P^\circ$ because the $m$ walls are equally spaced by $\theta$ and contain both boundary lines.

The finite chamber tiling. Assume $m<\infty$. The group $W_{s,t}=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle$ generated by the two involutions $\rho(s),\rho(t)$ whose product $A$ has exact order $m$ is a quotient of the dihedral group of order $2m$, so $|W_{s,t}|\le2m$; on the other hand its action on $P^*$ contains the rotation $A$ of order $m$ and the reflection $\rho(s)$ in the wall $H_{e_s}\cap P^*$ by 1.4 and 3.1, and these generate a group of order exactly $2m$ acting on the $2m$ sectors of 3.1, so $|W_{s,t}|=2m$ and $W_{s,t}$ is dihedral of order $2m$. The action maps the set of $m$ walls to itself, because $\rho(w)(H_\beta\cap P^*)=H_{\rho(w)\beta}\cap P^*$ and $\Phi_P$ is $W_{s,t}$-stable, so it permutes the $2m$ closed sectors; it maps the sector $C_P$ to the sectors obtained by successive rotations through $2\theta$ and by the reflection $\rho(s)$, which realizes all $2m$ of them, so the orbit of $C_P$ is exactly the set of closed sectors cut out by the $m$ root hyperplanes. Since $|W_{s,t}|=2m$ equals the number of sectors, the action on the orbit is simply transitive, and the sectors have pairwise disjoint interiors and union $P^*$ as the $2m$ sectors of $m$ distinct lines through the origin. Finally, any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane: choosing points $p,q$ in their interiors, the segment from $p$ to $q$ crosses some wall line $H_\beta\cap P^*$ (the interiors are different connected components of the complement of the union of the walls), and the two open half-planes of that line are convex and disjoint, so $p$ and $q$ lie in opposite open half-planes.
